candidate_relations.reason: Disseminated intravascular coagulation can produce cutaneous necrosis but is not the referenced pressure-induced auricular necrosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alternative systemic coagulopathic cause of skin necrosis

candidate_relations.reason: Calciphylaxis causes ischemic skin necrosis through vascular calcification and thrombosis, not pressure necrosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alternative vasculopathic cause of necrotic plaques

candidate_relations.reason: Vasculitis can cause necrotic cutaneous lesions but does not identify the referenced pressure necrosis, and the biopsy description does not report vasculitis.
Purpura fulminans is a systemic coagulopathic syndrome with hemorrhagic necrosis, distinct from localized pressure necrosis.
Sepsis may contribute to critical illness and vascular injury but is not the final diagnosis of the auricular lesions.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Associated systemic condition rather than the skin diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: Necrotizing fasciitis involves rapidly progressive fascial infection and is distinct from localized auricular pressure necrosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Deep soft-tissue infection rather than pressure injury

candidate_relations.reason: Coumadin necrosis is medication-induced thrombotic skin necrosis, not pressure necrosis; Coumadin exposure is not described.
Ecthyma gangrenosum is an infection-associated necrotic ulcer and represents a differential rather than pressure necrosis.
Warfarin-induced skin necrosis has a drug-mediated thrombotic etiology and is not the referenced pressure injury; warfarin exposure is not provided.
Septic emboli could be considered with bacteremia but are distinct from pressure necrosis and are not demonstrated in the biopsy.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alternative hematogenous vascular cause of necrotic lesions

candidate_relations.reason: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome causes widespread superficial epidermal splitting rather than localized pressure-related full-thickness auricular necrosis.
